title: Daru, Rav Nachman’s slave
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He is mentioned several times in the Talmud: in Pesachim 116a, where Rav Nachman said to him: a slave whose master frees him and gives him silver and gold — what ought he to say to him? Daru answered: He ought to give thanks and praise. Rav Nachman said to him: You have exempted us from saying 'Why is this night different'; and in Berakhot 13b, where Rav Nachman instructed him regarding the Shema: 'For the first verse, rouse me; beyond that, do not trouble me'; and in Shabbat 51a, where Rav Nachman said to him: 'Insulate cold water for me and bring me water heated by the Aramean cook'; and in Bava Kamma 97a, where Rava said of him: 'such as the case of Daru, the slave of Rav Nachman, who dances among wine barrels.' And in Dikdukei Soferim on Berakhot 13b the reading is that he was the slave of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, but that is an error, for he was the slave of Rav Nachman bar Yaakov, since in Shabbat 51a they say there that Rabbi Ami heard and became angry, and he lived in the time of Rav Nachman bar Yaakov, as is known.

notes.text: Hyman calls the questioner in Bava Kamma97a Rava; the checked William Davidson Hebrew witness reads Rabbah. Hyman also rejects Dikdukei Soferim’s Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak in favor of Rav Nachman bar Yaakov.

The consulted Daru passages preserve alternating actors: Nachman asks, Daru answers in Pesachim 116a; Berakhot 13b concerns rousing him for the first verse; Shabbat 51a names an Aramean cook heating water. Bava Kamma 97a has Rabbah, where Hyman says Rava. The DKS identification and chronology remain Hyman’s argument.
